summary: Stepped emergency offramp for optimizer config conflict causing tail latency spikes and intermittent 5xx errors
description:
Issue summary: BrightPost reports sharp tail-latency spikes (~95p to 99p) with intermittent 5xxs after a targeted optimizer rollout that enabled 'async_partitioned_batching' and a new quantization profile 'q8-dyn-lite'.
Impact: Customer-facing API errors for a subset of long-session chat requests; increased error rate from ~0.2% to ~3.7% for BrightPost traffic. Some streaming connections drop mid-response.
Observed behavior: Errors are concentrated on long sequences (>1k tokens) and large embedding+generation hybrid routes. Errors began at 2026-03-12T09:30 UTC shortly after a staged toggle of optimizer flags for the dedicated pool serving BrightPost.
Top-level ask: Provide a safe, stepped offramp to reduce customer impact (restore latency and eliminate 5xxs) while preserving telemetry to debug root cause.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightPost tenant credentials against prod us-east endpoint (tenant: brightpost-prod).
2) Run a mixed workload: 40% long-form chat (1k+ tokens), 40% short chat, 20% embedding+rerank calls using redwood-rl-13B pinned to optimizer profile 'alpha-experiment-2026-03-12'.
3) Observe tail latency and error rate over 10 minutes; compare to a control tenant pinned to 'stable-v2' profile.
4) Reproduce reliably by setting client-side concurrency to 12 connections and ensuring average input length > 600 tokens for long chat paths.
logs: [2026-03-12T09:33:21Z] serving-runtime ERROR tenant=brightpost pool=dedicated-12 request_id=aa1b... status=500 runtime=0.12s reason=kv-cache-evict-failed
[2026-03-12T09:34:02Z] optimizer WARN optimizer_profile=alpha-experiment-2026-03-12 flag=async_partitioned_batching step=3 evicted=842 lat_p95=1.8s
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: async_partitioned_batching interacts poorly with q8-dyn-lite quant profile on long-sequence KV cache patterns causing eviction churn and transient 5xxs.
Hypothesis B: The new quant profile reduces memory headroom on dedicated GPUs, triggering aggressive KV cache eviction and OOM-like failures surfaced as 5xxs rather than clear OOM logs.
Telemetry: GPU memory headroom dropped ~18% for impacted pods after 09:30 UTC; GC/eviction counters spiked in the same window.
Repro experiment: toggling async_partitioned_batching=false on a single replica reproduced tail latency improvement in 2/2 runs; error rate dropped to baseline.
Cross-checks: Other tenants on same pool but pinned to 'stable-v2' did not show errors, indicating tenant-level config gating is likely the trigger.
mitigation_and_workaround: Immediate mitigation (live): disable async_partitioned_batching at tenant scope for brightpost-prod. Command: rwctl tenant update-config --tenant brightpost-prod --set optimizer.async_partitioned_batching=false --reason 'emergency-offramp-2026-03-12'

If command unavailable: apply traffic-split in router to route BrightPost to a fallback pool pinned to 'stable-v2' (rwctl router set-split --tenant brightpost-prod --default-pool=fallback-stable --weight=100).
Short-term: increase KV cache size for brightpost tenant by +12% where resource headroom allows (rwctl tenant tune --tenant brightpost-prod --kv-cache-mb +12288).
Monitor: watch p95/p99 latencies, 5xx rate, and GPU memory headroom for 30 minutes post-change.
rollback_plan: Objective: perform a stepped, reversible rollback to restore baseline with minimal blast radius and preserve debug traces.
1) Pre-checks (owner: Miguel Torres): confirm snapshot of optimizer config and active routing. Command: rwctl tenant snapshot --tenant brightpost-prod --label 'pre-offramp-2026-03-12'
2) Step A (0-5 min): tenant-level toggle async_partitioned_batching=false for brightpost-prod. Validate 5xxs drop to <0.5% and p99 latency returns near baseline within 5m.
3) Step B (5-20 min): if Step A insufficient, revert quant profile to 'stable-q8' at tenant scope: rwctl tenant update-config --tenant brightpost-prod --set optimizer.quant_profile=stable-q8
4) Step C (if still degraded): shift 100% BrightPost traffic to fallback-stable pool and drain original pool replicas for deeper inspection.

5) Rollback validation: each step must have a 5m observation window with explicit GO/NO-GO from SRE and Customer Success. If GO, record timestamp and proceed. If NO-GO, roll back to previous step and notify customer.
6) Post-incident: capture heap/dump traces and upload to the secure S3 bucket per runbook. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Optimizer+Rollbacks+Playbook
Coordination: schedule change window with BrightPost CS at earliest possible (now), and post-mortem owner assigned. Notify #support and #incidents Slack channels with runbook link.
resolution: TBD - mitigation applied (async_partitioned_batching disabled) and monitoring in progress. Final verification pending 2-hour observation window.
follow_up_actions: 1) Post-mortem within 3 business days detailing root cause and long-term fix (owner: Miguel Torres).
2) Add automatic detection rule: if tenant tail_p99 > 1.5s AND kv_eviction_rate > 50/min after optimizer toggle, auto-disable async_partitioned_batching for that tenant (SRE task).
3) Test matrix: add long-session synthetic test to CI that runs against q8-dyn-lite + async_partitioned_batching to prevent regressions.
4) Document exact memory/eviction thresholds for quant profiles in the model catalog entry.
